title: Kabukcu et al. — Cooking in caves: Palaeolithic carbonised plant food remains from Franchthi and Shanidar
supports: Processed plant foods at Shanidar, Neanderthal layers around 70,000 years and Homo sapiens layers around 40,000 years; pounding/soaking, pulses, bitter or sharp ingredients.
limits: Flavour preference is an interpretation. Do not put Franchthi flatbread at Shanidar or at 50,000 years. No complete ancient recipe or universal diet is known from this study.

title: Miller & Wang — Ostrich eggshell beads reveal 50,000-year-old social network in Africa
supports: Ostrich eggshell ornaments in eastern and southern Africa and similarity interpreted as population connections over the last 50,000 years.
limits: No literal social media, follower numbers, individual wealth measure, or single recovered meaning of an ornament. Our necklace-choice scene is fictional. Avoid claiming a current oldest-known record.

title: Lozano et al. (2013) — Toothpicking and Periodontal Disease in a Neanderthal Specimen from Cova Foradà Site (Valencia, Spain)
supports: Two interproximal grooves consistent with repeated toothpicking; dental disease; proposed relief of discomfort.
limits: Specific Neanderthal specimen. Do not assign an unsupported exact 50,000-year date, present this as a universal routine, or infer modern dentistry. Drawings are generic schematics, not specimen photographs.

title: Wiessner (2014) — Embers of society: Firelight talk among the Ju/’hoansi Bushmen
supports: Study of 174 day/night conversations and 68 translated texts; daytime practical matters and social gossip, evening stories and social activities.
limits: Recent ethnography, not a transcript of prehistory or a universal model. Ju/’hoansi are contemporary people with histories, not unchanged ancestors. Do not use this to claim dopamine, internet addiction, or hardwired prehistoric scrolling.

title: Oktaviana et al. (2024) — Narrative cave art in Indonesia by 51,200 years ago
supports: Leang Karampuang, Sulawesi; minimum age of 51,200 years; human-like figures associated with a pig; authors' narrative interpretation.
limits: Minimum age, not exact painting date. Narrative is an attributed interpretation. No recovered words, plot, motive, or author. Do not repeat 2024 oldest-known superlatives as current records. Painted panel in this project is a schematic, not an exact reproduction.

title: Smith et al. (2017) — Cooperation and the evolution of hunter-gatherer storytelling
supports: Research among Agta communities: skilled storytellers preferred as social partners, narratives convey cooperation-related ideas.
limits: Modern study; associations and study results do not establish a specific 50,000-year-old scene or prove an immutable human brain. Do not depict these contemporary people as prehistoric.
